limitations: Controlled experiment on a bounded 1900 reconstruction, not a reconstruction of the 1888, 1897, 1904 or 1928 floods.
North and south boundaries are closed test boundaries. Only the two channel ends exchange water with prescribed reservoirs; the western reservoir is not a confirmed historical outfall.
Unsupported ground is estimated separately on each side from reviewed nearby field heights; its mask is retained. No modern ground or inherited flat scaffold is silently treated as surveyed terrain.
Road surface uses reviewed map spots; its profile is held at end values beyond the reviewed section inside this small domain.

Both local railway routes use a provisional common formation between 1.0 and 1.9 m ODN. At 1.6 m, the southern road bridge permits about 3.46 m below its assumed soffit to rail top. Grade between that bridge and this domain remains an assumption.
Drain sections, culvert roughness/losses and gate behaviour are assumed. The test pump is a sensitivity control, not the capacity or location of an identified historical pump.
Local-inertial surface flow omits advection, waves, sediment, sewer networks and infiltration. Do not use for fast dam-break flow or design.
The existing 3D landscape remains a separate visual reconstruction; this page uses the demo's corrected hydraulic surface.
